newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Nov trade deficit $145 mln - official.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Nov trade deficit $145 mln - official.

text.p: Argentina posted a trade deficit of $145 million in November, down from a $244 million shortfall in November 1995, the Economy Ministry said Tuesday.
But in the January-November period the country registered a $106 million surplus, compared with a $769 million surplus in the same period 1995.
Total foreign trade in the January-November period was $43.27 billion, a record, the ministry said.
In the 11 month period farm exports rose 15 percent, primary products 17 percent and fuel 36 percent, but industrial product shipments dropped two percent.

Imports over the same period rose across the board -- intermediate goods 16 percent, capital goods 17 percent, capital goods spare parts 17 percent, consumer goods 11 percent, buses 54 percent and fuel eight percent.
Total November exports were $1.92 billion, a 21 percent increase over November 1995, while imports were $2.06 billion, a 12 percent rise.
Total exports in the January-November period were $21.69 billion, a 12 percent increase, while imports were $21.58 billion, a 17 percent growth.
Trade with Mercosur customs union partners Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay posted a $1.85 billion surplus in the January-November period versus a $1.95 billion surplus a year earlier.
Trade deficit with the NAFTA trade block comprised by the United States, Canada and Mexico rose to $2.97 billion from a $2.58 billion shortfall a year earlier.
Trade with the European Union also registered a deficit, of $1.96 billion, up from a $1.42 billion shortfall over the same period 1995.
